about: How TandemNode controls a TandemLLM install without importing it: bin/tandem's verbs (exit 0 means done) and the install.sh flags the controller's installer runs. TandemNode never runs python -m server.* and never imports engine code.

install.source: the controller: TANDEM_ENGINE_INSTALL_SH, its ref Package.engine_ref() (proxy/nodeinstall.py)

stage.about: Since engine API 1.2: one stage of a split model. TandemNode writes these keys to each node's run/local.env (paths and IP literals only, never the key itself), starts the front first and the tail once the front's /health answers, and stops the tail first. ops/start.sh refuses a bad combination with exit 2 and one line '[start] REFUSING: ...' before any process starts.

keys.TANDEM_STAGE: LO:HI: 0:k the front, k:layers the tail
keys.TANDEM_LINK_LISTEN: IP:PORT (one of LISTEN and PEER on each stage; never a wildcard)
keys.TANDEM_LINK_KEY: the key file's path (mode 0600, at least 32 bytes, the same content on both nodes)
keys.TANDEM_STAGE_CACHES: on or off, equal on both
keys.QSE_PARALLEL: slots, equal on both (1 without caches)
keys.QSE_DISK_CACHE: off on the front; the tail's disk tier

chat.about: Since engine API 1.6: who runs chatd, the Chat tab's service, on an engine box. The engine's QSE_CHATD (run/local.env, or install.sh's line in run/ops/serve.env): node, TandemNode owns it: the launchers neither start nor stop it and say so, the watchdog leaves it alone, and bin/tandem chat runs tandem-node chat; off, nothing runs it. Up to 1.6, on (the default) meant the engine's launchers run it. Since 1.7 the engine has no chatd launcher at all: serve.env's mode block reads on as node (ops/start.sh says so in one line) and an unset or unknown value as off, so TandemNode sees node or off from a 1.7 engine. serve.env's engine mode keeps node and turns every other value off. An engine before 1.6 reads node as on, so TandemNode hands chatd over only to an engine whose /health says 1.6 or later within the same major, or that says off.
chat.engine_launcher: none since 1.7: ops/start.sh, ops/watchdog.sh, bin/tandem and install.sh never run a chatd launcher
chat.node_port: TANDEM_NODE_PORT, default 7700: ops/start.sh says whether a TandemNode answers there

watch.only_when: /health 200, no fresh .watchdog.off, not setup mode, not engine mode

install.about: Since 1.7: install.sh --with-chat --app-wheel FILE [--app-wheel-sha256 HEX] installs TandemApp's wheel (a local file) into the engine's venv with the engine's pins held, writes QSE_CHATD=node and QSE_MODE=chat, and writes TandemNode's systemd user unit (tandem-node unit --chat on --tandem-dir DIR); its sha256 is kept in DIR/state/tandemapp-wheel.json. --with-chat with no wheel keeps a TandemApp this install already has, else stops and says where to get one.
install.node_bin: DIR/venv/bin/tandem-node; bin/tandem node and bin/tandem chat run it (TANDEM_NODE_BIN first, then the venv's, then PATH)

chat.update: Since 1.7: an install from before 1.7 runs its own copies (run/ops/*.sh, run/ops/serve.env, bin/tandem) until install.sh writes them again. A re-run of install.sh on such an install in chat mode whose chatd the engine ran (QSE_CHATD on or unset) stops before it changes anything, unless it is told --with-chat --app-wheel FILE (TandemNode takes chatd over: the same data folder, pid file and port) or --engine-only; --runtime-only never writes them.
